case_title: Pattu Rajan v. State of Tamil Nadu
accused_occupation: Proprietor of a chain of hotels (Accused No. 1); other accused's occupations not stated
accused_socioeconomic_status: Accused No. 1 described as proprietor of a hotel chain and as giving costly gifts and financial help; no explicit statement of wealth class for others
accused_victim_relationship: Prior connection/prior enmity: Accused No. 1 sought to marry the victim's wife (PW1) and committed the murder to remove the victim as an obstacle
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.364, s.201 (trial court convicted under s.364, s.304 Part I and s.201; High Court altered s.304 Part I to s.302)
weapon: Ligature (lungi) used for strangulation; no weapon recovered as such
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence; ocular testimony of PW1 and PW2 (wife and mother-in-law); last seen; motive; recovery on confession; identification of body; expert superimposition evidence; medical (post-mortem); documentary (hotel records, petrol pump bills)
confession: Accused No. 2's statement to police (in presence of VAO PW7) leading to disposal site; only the portion leading to recovery was relied on under s.27. Accused No. 6's confession led to recovery of wallet and gold chain, relied on
aggravating_circumstances: Planned elimination of the victim to marry his wife; instruction to 'finish him off'; body dumped in forest; the murder was intended to permanently remove the victim
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.364, 304 Part I and 201; sentence not stated in judgment
high_court_outcome: Appeals by accused and State; guilt confirmed; conviction under s.304 Part I altered to s.302 IPC
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 (murder), as modified by the High Court; the trial court's convictions under s.364 and s.201 were not disturbed
neutral_facts: The accused sought to take the wife of the victim as a third wife, and over time tried to separate the couple through gifts, financial help and interference in their personal lives. On 01.10.2001 the victim and his wife were abducted and released the same day, and a separate complaint was lodged about that abduction. On 26.10.2001 the wife and victim were taken in a vehicle from Tirunelveli, accompanied by several co-accused. At a culvert on the way, co-accused alighted from a following vehicle and took the victim away, and the accused reportedly instructed them to finish him off. The victim's body was found on 31.10.2001 in a forest area near Kodaikanal, decomposed, and was buried as unidentified. The wife said she was under surveillance and could not file a complaint earlier. Investigation included a confession by one accused who led police to the body and a recovery of the body on that basis; recovery of a wallet and gold chain from another accused's house; identification of the body by the wife and family from photographs, clothes, belongings and a scar on the waist; a superimposition test by an expert; post-mortem findings of death by throttling and a broken hyoid bone; handwriting comparison of hotel records; and petrol pump bills showing the vehicle refuelled en route to Kodaikanal. The victim was last seen with the accused.
physical_harm: Death by asphyxia due to throttling; hyoid bone broken (ante-mortem)
number_of_offences: 3 charged; 3 finally upheld (s.302 as modified, s.364, s.201)
premeditation_planning: Court found murder was intended to permanently remove the victim; a series of attempts to sever the marriage preceded it; no express premeditation finding beyond this
motive: Accused No. 1 wanted to take PW1 as his third wife and eliminated the victim to marry her without obstruction (accepted by courts below and by Supreme Court)
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PW1 and PW2 on motive, last seen, identification; s.27 recovery of body on accused No. 2's information; recovery of wallet and gold chain on accused No. 6's confession; identification by photographs, clothes, belongings and scar; superimposition test (PW34); petrol pump bills; hotel handwriting report (PW36)
witness_credibility: PW1 and PW2 found natural, consistent, cogent and steadfast; minor variations held not to affect the case; other witnesses (PW7, 26, 27, 29, 32, 33) found homogeneous and reliable
post_offence_conduct: Accused surrendered and confessed; Accused No. 2 led police to the disposal site; Accused No. 6 led police to wallet and gold chain; no explanation given under s.313 for last seen circumstance
trial_duration: offence: 26.10.2001; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 19.03.2009; Supreme Court: 29.03.2019
legal_representation: For appellants: Sushil Kumar, Senior Advocate (with others); for State: Balaji Srinivasan, Additional Advocate General
investigation_status: FIR registered 20.11.2001 (Crime No. 1047 of 2001); body found and post-mortem conducted; charges framed; trial conducted; chargesheet filing not expressly stated
procedural_irregularity: None noted; defence objections on second FIR, use of prior FIR (Ext. P3) and s.313 non-putting of last seen evidence were rejected by the Court
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted (ss.364, 304 Part I, 201); High Court: guilt confirmed, s.304 Part I altered to s.302; Supreme Court: appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Supported the findings of the trial court and High Court; evidence of PW1 and PW2, motive, last seen, recovery and superimposition identification were proved
defence_argument: Second FIR impermissible as continuation of abduction; motive not proved; recovery shaky; last seen not put under s.313; superimposition improper without DNA test; circumstances proved on assumptions
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence panchsheel (chain complete, excludes other hypotheses); separate FIR permissible for distinct offence; DNA and superimposition are opinion evidence, not binding; last seen doctrine shifts burden
precedent_relied_upon: State of A.P. v. Cheemalapati Ganeswara Rao [1964] 3 SCR 297; T.T. Antony v. State of Kerala (2001) 6 SCC 181; Awadesh Kumar Jha v. State of Bihar (2016) 3 SCC 8; Rameshchandra Nandlal Parikh (2006) 1 SCC 732; Nirmal Singh Kahlon (2009) 1 SCC 441; Babubhai v. State of Gujarat (2010) 12 SCC 254; Sharad Birdhichand Sarda (1984) 4 SCC 116; Ramesh Chandra Agrawal (2009) 9 SCC 709; Shankar v. State of TN (1994) 4 SCC 478; Mahesh Dhanaji Shinde (2014) 4 SCC 292; Rohtash Kumar (2013) 14 SCC 434; Inder Singh (1978) 4 SCC 161

case_title.quote: PATTU RAJAN v. THE STATE OF TAMIL NADU

number_of_accused.quote: On 26.10.2001, at about 6.30 a.m., Accused No. 5 came to the room

accused_occupation.quote: Accused No. 1 is the proprietor of a chain of hotels (Saravana Bhavan).

accused_socioeconomic_status.quote: gave her costly gifts such as jewellery and silk sarees and even went to the extent of paying her medical bills

victim_gender.quote: the murder of one Santhakumar, husband of the complainant Jeevajothi (PW1)

accused_victim_relationship.quote: Accused No. 1 had evinced a keen desire to take PW1 as his third wife, though she was already married to Santhakumar (the deceased).

offence_category.quote: the abduction and murder of one Santhakumar

statutory_provisions.quote: Charges were framed under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as "the IPC") including Sections 302, 364 and 201

weapon.quote: strangulation of the said person by using materials like a lungi

evidence_type.quote: Clearly, there is no direct evidence in this matter and the whole case rests on circumstantial evidence.

confession.quote: if a confession is made by the accused before the police and a portion of the confession leads to the recovery of any incriminating material, such portion alone is admissible under Section 27

aggravating_circumstances.quote: Accused No. 1 further instructed these accused to "finish him off"

trial_court_outcome.quote: The Trial Court, upon evaluation of the material on record, convicted the accused appellants for the offences punishable under Sections 364, 304 Part I and 201 of the IPC.

high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court while confirming the finding of guilt of the accused, modified the conviction for the offence punishable under Section 304 Part I to Section 302 of the IPC.

final_outcome.quote: Thus, the judgment of the Trial Court as modified by the High Court need not be interfered with. Hence these appeals fail and stand dismissed.

offence_finally_established.quote: the judgment of the Trial Court as modified by the High Court need not be interfered with.

neutral_facts.quote: On 26.10.2001, at about 6.30 a.m., Accused No. 5 came to the room in which PW1 and her family members were staying in Tirunelveli

attempt_completion.quote: the offence of abduction was completed on 01.10.2001 itself

physical_harm.quote: the cause of death was found to be asphyxia due to throttling

number_of_offences.quote: Charges were framed under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as "the IPC") including Sections 302, 364 and 201

premeditation_planning.quote: the intention behind the second offence was to murder the deceased with a view to permanently get rid of him

motive.quote: the motive for commission of the offence had been proved

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the overwhelming, consistent, cogent and reliable testimonies of PWs 1 and 2, along with the aforementioned corroborative evidence, conclusively prove the prosecution case.

witness_credibility.quote: We do not find any embellishment or exaggeration in the evidence of these witnesses.

post_offence_conduct.quote: Meanwhile, the accused had surrendered and confessed to the commission of Santhakumar's murder.

trial_duration.quote: On 26.10.2001, at about 6.30 a.m., Accused No. 5 came to the room

legal_representation.quote: Balaji Srinivasan, AAG , Sushil Kumar, Sr. Adv., Ms. Aishwarya Bhati

investigation_status.quote: she lodged the first information on 20.11.2001 stating that Accused No.1 and his henchmen had murdered her husband, and the same was registered as Crime No.1047 of 2001.

procedural_irregularity.quote: we have no hesitation in holding that the separate first information lodged in this case is just, legal and proper.

appeal_history.quote: The accused appellants as well as the State appealed before the High Court, wherein the High Court while confirming the finding of guilt of the accused, modified the conviction

prosecution_argument.quote: Shri Balaji Srinivasan, the learned Additional Advocate General appearing on behalf of the State, argued in support of the judgments of the Courts below.

defence_argument.quote: the first information in the present case (Ext. P1) registered on 20.11.2001 could not have been registered at all, inasmuch as there cannot be a second FIR relating to the same incident.

legal_principle_applied.quote: The Judge while deciding matters resting on circumstantial evidence should always tread cautiously so as to not allow conjectures or suspicion, however strong, to take the place of proof.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: (See State of A.P. v. Cheemalapati Ganeswara Rao , (1964) 3 SCR 297)
